For each fixed R>1, J_n is the leading principal submatrix of J_(n+1). Equality of their smallest eigenvalues would make a minimizing eigenvector extended by zero an eigenvector of the larger matrix; its last row and backward recurrence force every coordinate to vanish. Thus z_(n+1)<z_n. The quadratic-form lower bound and alternating unit-vector upper bound give -2<z_n<=-2+(2-delta)/n, including n=1, and therefore z_n decreases to -2. Mapping through arccos(sqrt((B+z)/A)) makes the largest lower-half phase increase to phi. The analytically established root ordering identifies the actual adjacent ratio, and the negative derivative of (pi/y-1)^2 proves strict decrease and the stated limit for every n.
